messages.content:
You are an expert synthetic chemist planning experiments to maximise reaction yield.
Each experiment chooses one option for every variable listed. You will see the results
of experiments already run. Choose the next batch to find the highest-yield conditions
in as few experiments as possible. Use chemical knowledge (ligand and base effects,
substrate reactivity, solvent effects) and the observed results. Balance exploiting
good regions with testing informative new combinations. Never repeat an experiment.
Return JSON only.

Pd-catalysed direct C-H arylation of an imidazole to form 5-(2-fluorophenyl)-1-methyl-1H-imidazole-4-carbonitrile (Shields et al., Nature 2021, reaction 3); choose the base, ligand, solvent, concentration and temperature.

Variables and options:
base:
B1: Base option 1
B2: Base option 2
B3: Base option 3
B4: Base option 4

ligand:
L1: Ligand option 1
L2: Ligand option 2
L3: Ligand option 3
L4: Ligand option 4
L5: Ligand option 5
L6: Ligand option 6
L7: Ligand option 7
L8: Ligand option 8
L9: Ligand option 9
L10: Ligand option 10
L11: Ligand option 11
L12: Ligand option 12

solvent:
S1: Solvent option 1
S2: Solvent option 2
S3: Solvent option 3
S4: Solvent option 4

concentration:
C1: Concentration option 1
C2: Concentration option 2
C3: Concentration option 3

temperature:
T1: Temperature option 1
T2: Temperature option 2
T3: Temperature option 3

Experiments so far (best first):
B3 | L8 | S3 | C2 | T3 -> 88.8%
B3 | L8 | S3 | C2 | T2 -> 82.3%
B2 | L8 | S3 | C2 | T2 -> 76.7%
B3 | L8 | S3 | C2 | T1 -> 58.0%
B3 | L8 | S4 | C2 | T2 -> 45.0%
B2 | L1 | S1 | C2 | T3 -> 28.5%
B4 | L12 | S1 | C2 | T2 -> 7.3%
B2 | L7 | S2 | C3 | T2 -> 0.2%
B3 | L6 | S2 | C1 | T3 -> 0.0%
B3 | L1 | S3 | C2 | T2 -> 0.0%

Propose exactly 5 NEW experiments not listed above. Return JSON:
{"picks": [{"base": "<label>", "ligand": "<label>", "solvent": "<label>", "concentration": "<label>", "temperature": "<label>", "reason": "<one sentence>"}]}

picks.reason: Retains the best-performing base, ligand, solvent, and temperature while testing whether lower concentration improves the strong lead condition.
Tests the other untried concentration under the established high-yield conditions to identify a concentration optimum.
B2 was competitive with B3 at T2, so testing it at the best temperature checks whether it can match or exceed the lead.
Screens an untested base while holding the highly successful ligand, solvent, concentration, and temperature constant.
Checks whether the poorer S4 result at T2 was temperature-dependent while preserving the best-performing base and ligand.
